practices_evaluation.justification: The test contains two distinct 'Act' operations: constructing a Grafo instance (new Grafo()) and then invoking a method on a null reference inside a try-catch (g.toString()). That means multiple behaviors are exercised in the same test instead of a single Arrange-Act-Assert block.
The test uses only local variables and there is a @Before/@After skeleton present in the class to support independent initialization/cleanup. No shared mutable state is modified in this method.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Coverage of Normal and Exceptional Flows
practices_evaluation.justification: The class contains only a single test method. Although the test includes an in-method try/catch to exercise a NullPointerException, the decision rules require separate test methods for happy and error paths; there is not a distinct exception test using the testing framework mechanisms.

The test validates construction and a null-invocation path; there are no input ranges or numeric/string boundaries being exercised here, so boundary-value analysis is not applicable to this specific test.

The test class does not extract reusable helper methods or constants. There is duplicated inline structure (construct + assert) and no helper methods despite potential reuse. The method is not very small and contains an extra exceptional exercise inline rather than modularized.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Detailed Analysis of Size and Complexity
practices_evaluation.justification: The test method is relatively small (no loops or complex conditionals). It has simple linear flow and a single try/catch; it does not exceed complexity thresholds (no loops, no nested conditions).
The test contains a single substantive assertion (assertNotNull). It does not verify multiple properties of the Grafo instance or other behaviors, so assertions are superficial and may miss faults.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Rigorous Use of Performance and Security Tests
practices_evaluation.justification: The test uses @Test(timeout = 4000), an explicit timeout-based check which is a performance-related assertion per the decision rules, so the presence of a timing constraint is noted as compliant for this practice.

The method name is generic ('test0') and does not follow descriptive naming conventions. Although there is a Javadoc comment with description, the naming decision rule requires descriptive method names.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Small Footprint of Test Code Generation
practices_evaluation.justification: The test shows clear signs of automated generation: class name 'EvoAITest', EvoSuite imports and runner annotations, and a generic test method name 'test0'. This indicates heavy code generation patterns rather than minimal focused tests.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Complete Prioritization of Test Case Design
practices_evaluation.justification: The test includes a Given/When/Then comment block and a requirement id (REQ-001), indicating thought-out design and intent rather than an ad-hoc test.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Responsible Addition of Test Code Maintenance
practices_evaluation.justification: The test interacts only with the public constructor and public methods; there is no reflection or access to private fields. The test verifies observable behavior via public API.

The primary assertion includes a descriptive failure message (assertNotNull with message). While there's only one assertion, it uses a specific assertion with a message, meeting the rule that a significant portion of assertions include messages.
The test contains concise Given/When/Then comments and a Javadoc describing the requirement; there is no excessive or commented-out code, so comments add value and explain intent.

The test avoids non-deterministic sources (no Random, no time-based calls, no Thread.sleep) and uses only deterministic operations. The EvoRunner parameterization is class-level but the method itself is deterministic.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Complete Avoidance of Test Side Effects
practices_evaluation.justification: The test does not modify global state, create files, or persist data; it operates on local variables and includes @Before/@After placeholders for potential cleanup, so no side effects are evident.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Suitable Utilization of Test Labels and Categories
practices_evaluation.justification: The class has only one test method. Per the decision rules, when a class contains only one or two tests, labeling/categorization is considered not-applicable rather than strictly non-compliant.
